<!-- Keep related work together. Smaller, focused changes are easier to review;
     a larger coherent change does not need artificial splitting. -->

## What changed

<!-- Start with the problem and resulting behavior. Order changes by impact.
     Link the issue this fixes, e.g. "Fixes #123", and list any dependencies the change needs. -->

## Type of change

<!-- Delete options that are not relevant. -->

- [ ] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)
- [ ] New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality)
- [ ] Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to not work as expected)
- [ ] This change requires a documentation update

## Why

<!-- Explain the reason or meaningful tradeoff without repeating the opening. -->

## How it works

<!-- One simple diagram when a flow, state change or structure is hard to picture:
     a Mermaid chart (GitHub renders it) or an image. Few boxes, plain-word labels,
     one idea, and a one-line caption saying what to notice.
     Remove this section when the prose already makes it obvious. -->

## UI changes

<!-- Show only changed behavior. Pair running-app captures of the same screen,
     state and viewport. Add a short video for motion or interaction changes.
     Remove this section when nothing visible changes. -->

## Verification

<!-- Checks actually run and results, plus material coverage limits.
     Link long evidence. Distinguish suggested reproduction from completed checks.
     Give the steps to reproduce and any relevant test configuration. -->

## Risk

<!-- Include material remaining risks, compatibility or rollout considerations.
     Remove this section when it adds no information. -->

## Checklist

- [ ] The scope is focused; related changes belong together
- [ ] I explained what changed and why
- [ ] I included before/after images for visible changes
- [ ] I included a video for motion or interaction changes
- [ ] My code follows the style guidelines of this project
- [ ] I have performed a self-review of my own code
- [ ] I have commented my code, particularly in hard-to-understand areas
- [ ] I have made corresponding changes to the documentation
- [ ] My changes generate no new warnings
- [ ] I have added tests that prove my fix is effective or that my feature works
- [ ] New and existing unit tests pass locally with my changes
- [ ] Any dependent changes have been merged and published in downstream modules

<!-- Replace inapplicable media checkboxes with a plain N/A note and reason. -->
